summary:
### TL;DR
- Secret scanning can now find secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs. It is in public preview, off by default, and enterprise owners on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with GitHub Secret Protection or GitHub Advanced Security can turn it on. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-09-secret-scanning-detects-secrets-in-github-actions-workflow-logs))
- During the preview, alerts from workflow logs **do not send notifications**. You have to check the repository's secret scanning alert list yourself. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-09-secret-scanning-detects-secrets-in-github-actions-workflow-logs))
- The AI Scan for repositories docs now say that self-hosted runners are not supported. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-scan-for-repositories))

### Action required
Nothing this time.

### Security improvements
- **Secret scanning for Actions workflow logs (public preview)** ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-09-secret-scanning-detects-secrets-in-github-actions-workflow-logs))
  - **How it works:** Logs are scanned for provider patterns when a workflow run completes. Findings show up in the repository's secret scanning alert list, with a link back to the workflow log.
  - **Validity and retention:** Validity checks run for supported secret types. Alerts stay available even after the logs are deleted.
  - **Who can use it:** Enterprises on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with GitHub Secret Protection or GitHub Advanced Security, including data residency on GHE.com.
  - **How to enable:** In enterprise settings, go to **Policies → Advanced Security** and set the "All repositories" dropdown to **Enabled**. The policy is disabled by default and only applies to repositories that already have secret scanning enabled under those licenses.
  - **Preview limitations:**
    - Only runs that finish after you enable the feature are scanned. Existing logs are not backfilled.
    - Generic patterns, custom patterns, AI-detected secrets, and secrets already masked by Actions are not detected.
    - Alerts generate no notifications, so if you enable it, plan to review the alert list manually.

### Docs changes worth reading
- **AI Scan for repositories: self-hosted runners not supported** ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/ai-scan-for-repositories), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/3419465fe57aaf6bfe0bdfe22b7294cb9d3b6878))
  - "Self-hosted runners are not supported" was added to the Limitations section. The other limitations are unchanged:
    - Scans cover the default branch only.
    - Scans are triggered manually.
    - Scans are not exhaustive.
    - CodeQL alert matching is best effort.
  - The rest of the commit was a whitespace fix.

changelog.title: Secret scanning detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs
changelog.text: GitHub secret scanning now detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs, in addition to issues, wikis, discussions, and pull requests . Actions workflow log scanning is available in public preview. How does Actions workflow log scanning work? When a workflow run completes, GitHub scans its logs for provider patterns. Findings appear in your repository’s secret scanning alert list, alongside alerts from code and other content, with a link back to the Actions workflow log. Validity checks run for supported secret types, and alerts remain available even after the logs are deleted. How do I enable it? The preview is available to enterprises on GitHub Enterprise Cloud with GitHub Secret Protection or GitHub Advanced Security, including those with data residency on GHE.com. Enterprise owners can enable Secret scanning for Actions workflow logs by opening their enterprise settings and selecting Policies , then Advanced Security . Select Enabled in the All repositories dropdown. The policy is disabled by default and applies only to repositories with secret scanning enabled under those licenses. What should I know about the preview? Only workflow runs that complete after you enable the feature are scanned; existing logs aren’t backfilled. Generic patterns, custom patterns, AI-detected secrets, and secrets already masked by Actions aren’t detected. Alerts from Actions workflow logs don’t generate notifications during the preview, so check your repository’s secret scanning alert list directly. Learn more Learn more about secret scanning in our product documentation. Have feedback? Let us know by joining the discussion . We’re listening. The post Secret scanning detects secrets in GitHub Actions workflow logs appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

 ## Limitations
 
 * Scans analyze the default branch only.
+* Self-hosted runners are not supported.
 * Scans are manually triggered. Scheduled scans and automatic scans on push are not supported.
 * The agent selects which code to examine within a time budget. A scan does not exhaustively analyze every file or guarantee that it finds every vulnerability.
 * Matching against existing {% data variables.product.prodname_codeql %} alerts is best effort, so duplicate alerts can occur.
